answer: One workable design: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because pigment only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, hollow is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any terrace approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
